newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT struggling to meet ISDN demand.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT struggling to meet ISDN demand.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV said on Thursday ballooning demand for digital Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) lines meant subscribers could have to wait up to seven weeks for a line.

A spokesman said the firm had had an ambitious blueprint to swell ISDN services this year but had been surprised by a surge in demand as private users and small businesses clamoured for the high-capacity lines to connect to the Internet.
"There's an enormous demand for ISDN at the moment, more than we expected, and that's basically because demand for access to the Internet is so great," the spokesman said.

Dutch PTT spokesman Mark Zellenrath said digital ISDN technology allows users to increase the speed and capacity of their existing analogue connections, enabling them to take phone calls while online on the Internet.
Digital compression of data means ISDN lines can also handle Internet traffic five times faster than analogue lines, he said.

Zellenrath said Dutch PTT started out in 1996 with some 25,000 ISDN lines and planned to grow this to around 100,000 by the end of the year. "Halfway through the year we had 50,000 connections and right now we have around 75,000, and by the end of the year we will have much more than 100,000," he said.
Dutch PTT faced a shortage of engineers trained specifically to install ISDN and was working on training more, either in house or with contractors, he said.
Dutch phone users were opting for ISDN lines because they were cheaper than subscribing to a second analogue line, but still allowed two lines to be open at once, said Zellenrath.

He said Dutch PTT's problems over ISDN centred on the two-line package, while demand for its 30-line package aimed at big business users was manageable. Zellenrath declined to comment on industry projections that ISDN lines would top 225,000 by the end of next year.
